title: Outpatient Appointment Scheduling
notes:
Discovery workshop — Outpatient appointment scheduling — 3 Feb 2026

Dr. Fiona Marsh (Clinical Director): Across our nine clinics we still book appointments over the phone into a shared paper diary at each site, and double-bookings happen most weeks. Patients need to be able to book, reschedule, and cancel appointments online.

Tom Reilly (Operations Manager): Online booking should show real-time availability per clinician, not just per clinic — some of our consultants split time across two sites.

Ben Coulson (Patient Services Manager): We get a lot of no-shows, especially for first appointments. Ideally the system sends an SMS and email reminder 48 hours before the appointment, and again 2 hours before.

Dr. Fiona Marsh (Clinical Director): Any patient record has to pull from our NHS Spine lookup to confirm the NHS number before the first appointment is confirmed — we can't have a booking without a verified NHS number, that's a hard requirement from the trust.

Aisha Patel (IT Lead): Our practice management system is EMIS. Appointment data needs to sync with EMIS both ways — a booking made online should show in EMIS, and if a clinician blocks time in EMIS, it should disappear from the online slots.

Tom Reilly (Operations Manager): Cancellations within 24 hours of the appointment should free the slot for another patient automatically, but we also want to flag those patients so reception can follow up — persistent late-cancellers are a real problem for us.

Dr. Fiona Marsh (Clinical Director): Under UK GDPR, patient data has to stay within the UK, and we need an audit trail of who viewed which patient record and when — that's something our last CQC inspection specifically asked about.

Ben Coulson (Patient Services Manager): We'd like patients to be able to request a specific clinician, though for some clinic types like physiotherapy, ideally the system should also let them just book "next available" instead.

Aisha Patel (IT Lead): On performance, we're targeting under 3 seconds to load the available slots for any given clinic, even during the Monday morning rush when everyone's trying to book at once.

Tom Reilly (Operations Manager): Referrals from GPs are out of scope for this project — those still come through the existing e-Referral Service process, we're only building patient self-service booking for existing patients.

Dr. Fiona Marsh (Clinical Director): We need at least seven years of appointment and attendance history retained, in line with NHS records retention guidance.

Ben Coulson (Patient Services Manager): Honestly the phone lines get so backed up on Monday mornings that patients just give up and walk into A&E instead, which isn't great for anyone.

Tom Reilly (Operations Manager): We've been told this needs to go live before the new financial year starts in April, and the board has capped the budget at £180,000 for this phase.
